findings.class_imbalance: Extreme class skew: Fraud comprises only 1.80% (90 cases) against 4910 legitimate transactions. Standard accuracy would yield ~98.2% by naively predicting all legitimate, necessitating Precision-Recall evaluation and SMOTE/class-weight balancing.
findings.amount_distribution: Fraudulent transactions average $236.76, significantly higher than legitimate transactions ($57.03). Fraud exhibits a bimodal signature: micro card-testing charges (<$10) followed by larger burst amounts ($250-$2,000).
findings.temporal_velocity: Fraud probability peaks during off-peak night windows (Hours 2:00 - 5:00, reaching 6.9%), when automated fraud scripts exploit delayed cardholder alerting.

correlation_analysis.summary: Features V14, V12, V10 exhibit strong negative correlations with fraud, while V4, V11, V2 show strong positive correlations.
